title: CO0587 - Essex ActivAte Programme (HAF) 2025
description:
The Department for Education has provided Essex County Council with funding in order to deliver the holiday activity and food programme (HAF) across Essex during the Easter, Summer and Winter school holidays. Active Essex will be managing the programme on behalf of Essex County Council. Active Essex and Essex County Council will also be managing the HAF programme on behalf of Thurrock Council. Across Essex and Thurrock the programme is called Essex ActvAte. \r
\r
Essex ActivAte will engage and support young people and families who are eligible for benefits based free school meals and families most in need. The programme will provide free and inclusive holiday clubs across the county that will include a range of fun physical and enrichment activities, a free nutritious meal, nutritional education and mentoring and support for the young person and whole family. The programme aims to improve health generally, including, crucially, mental health and aim to provide the families with the knowledge and support to live healthier, happier lives.  \r
\r
We are looking for delivery partners or consortiums who can lead and deliver Essex ActivAte clubs across Essex and Thurrock during the main school holidays.  \r
\r
The Essex ActivAte programme has now been running for 3 years, working with over 300 delivery partners to offer over 150,000 free spaces and hot meals per year. Over the next year of 2025, it is our aim to extend the programme so that every young person who is eligible for benefits based free school meals or is in need of this holiday support has the opportunity to engage in a local club. \r
\r
Key outcomes of each Essex ActivAte club are:\r
â€¢	To provide free and inclusive holiday activity clubs for eligible young people\r
â€¢	To provide a safe environment for young people to attend in the school holidays\r
â€¢	To provide a fun, high quality holiday club experience for the young people\r
â€¢	To support the social skills of the young people attending\r
â€¢	To provide mentors and role model through the Essex ActivAte club staff\r
â€¢	To ensure that young people have at least 1 nutritious meal each day\r
â€¢	To provide education for the young people and whole family around eating more healthy, nutritious meals, on a budget\r
â€¢	Providing signposting and support for the whole family so that they have the understanding and knowledge to improve their physical and mental health and wellbeing, support network and opportunities. \r
\r
The maximum bid value per project is £300,000.

title: 1057 Energy Switching Partner for the 'Essex Energy Switch'
description:
Essex County Council is looking to offer collective energy switching services to households and businesses in Essex by engaging a Contractor to operate the Essex Energy Switch Service and support the Council in its aim to reduce fuel poverty within the County of Essex. \r
The Contractor is expected to develop, promote and manage the Essex Energy Switch Service on behalf of the Council, so households and businesses in Essex could:  \r
- Switch gas and/or electricity providers  \r
- Reduce energy costs based on their individual circumstances. \r
- Access electricity tariffs which are 100% provided by renewable energy. \r
\r
Interested contractors can assess this opportunity via the Council's e-sourcing portal, ProContract: https://procontract.due-north.com/Login. Log in as a Supplier and search the following: DN694199 / 1057 Energy Switching Partner for the 'Essex Energy Switch'.\r
\r
If you do not have an account, registration is free of charge at https://procontract.due-north.com/Register and it provides access to all current and forthcoming procurement opportunities for Essex County Council alongside several other public sector organisations.\r
\r
Tender submission must be done electronically, by publishing through this ITT 1057 Energy Switching Partner for the 'Essex Energy Switch' at: https://procontract.due-north.com/Login - reference DN694199; Not later than 12 noon hours on 14th March,2025. It is the Council's policy to reject any tender received after the above deadline.

title: Children and Young People&apos;s Mental Health Service (CAMHS) for Southend, Essex and Thurrock
description:
The purpose of this Notice is to confirm the award of a contract to North East London NHS Foundation
Trust (NELFT) to provide Children and Young People&apos;s Mental Health Services (CAMHS) across Southend,
Essex and Thurrock. This award is being made following the successful completion of a procurement
process.

The contract advert (Find a Tender reference 2021/S 000-009636) was published by NHS West Essex Clinical
Commissioning Group (CCG) on behalf of the 7 CCGs within Essex and the 3 Local Authorities. Since this
contract notice was published, the CCGs have been replaced with 3 Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) in line with the
Health and Care Act 2022.  The contract is led by Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB with the following organisations associates to the contract: Suffolk and North East Essex ICB, Mid and South Essex ICB, Southend Borough Council, Essex County Council and Thurrock Council.

The contract began on 1st April 2022 for a period of 7-years with the option to extend for a further 3-
years. The aggregate maximum value of the contract is £430m. The total price for the initial 7-year period
is £154,885,967.

The Thrive Model has been developed nationally. This has been endorsed by the &apos;Future in Mind&apos; report,
it is therefore the intention to replicate a version of the Thrive Model in delivering the new service. The
model is a blend of Tier 2 and Tier 3 services with a seamless progression up or down for the service
user.

All children and families will receive support and services which are appropriate to their needs. For many
children this is likely to be community based, and should be easily and quickly accessible. Most young
people requiring CAMHS will present with mental health problems that are causing significant
impairments in their day-to-day lives. These presentations can result in both the need for scheduled
and/or unscheduled care.

CAMHS will be available for all children and young people who are aged 0 - 18 (25 if SEND), and who
meet the agreed CAMHS referral criteria. The eligibility criteria is set out within the service specification.

As a part of the contract North East Essex have commissioned an additional Children and Young People&apos;s
Mental Health Early Intervention Service (CYP EIS).

description:

\r
Lot 1: Property Insurance (comprising buildings and contents that the Council are responsible for and includes maintained schools)\r
\r
Lot 2: Motor Insurance (comprising general fleet and waste vehicles)\r
\r
Lot 3: School Journeys (travel) Insurance (for all maintained schools. The policy covers all authorised personnel on official schools trips for personal accident and travel.)\r
\r
Lot 4: Engineering Inspection Insurance (for all relevant plant in ECC buildings and maintained schools.)\r
\r
Each Lot will be awarded to a single supplier for the contract duration. Each contract will be for an initial term of 3 years (commencing 1st April 2025), with an option to extend for up to a further 2 years (12 month increments each).\r
\r
Bidders must also note that the contracts are for provision of Insurance Policy Services only. The Council's broker service is contracted to a third party provider who are supporting this tender procedure.

title: CO0570 Systemic Training - Adult & Children & Families Services ESCA
description:
Systemic social work is a way of responding to family problems by recognising that we are all part of complex systems.\r
\r
Essex County Council's Children and Families (C&F) service overarching approach is relationship based, within this we use four main theoretical models; Systemic Practice, Solution Focused Practice, Strengths Based Approach and Restorative Practice.  These four models provide practitioners with the skills and knowledge to deliver relationship based social work practice in Essex. Please refer to Appendix A Our Vision and Values for Children and Families.\r
\r
Essex County Council's Adult Social Care (ASC) is one of the first County Councils nationally to adopt the Systemic Practice model into ASC. Systemic Practice is one of the 3 key elements of ASC's Practice Model, we have named Inclusive Essex. This also includes Trauma Informed Practice and being Strengths-Based. This helps all staff in Adult Social Care.  As of 2024 Systemic practice also forms part of our mandatory CPD offer to ASC staff called our 'Essentials Programme' \r
\r
The scope of the Systemic Training course is to deliver courses with Adults Social Care workforce and Children and Families workforce.\r
\r
The requirement has been split into the following Lots.\r
Lot 1 -Systemic Training for Children & Families and Adults\r
Lot 2 - Systemic Strategic Training for Leadership and Management across ASC & C&F\r
\r
Lot 1 (A) Children and Families\r
\r
Within the C&F services most of our training courses run face to face and are to be held centrally at County Hall, Chelmsford. ESCA will organise and finance venues for the training to take place. The only session the Children and Families service require to be delivered virtually is Team Manager Group Supervision.\r
\r
The target audience for this training course will be alternatively qualified workers, qualified social workers, senior practitioners, team & service managers, heads of service and directors from Children and Families.  \r
\r
The aim of the training programme is to upskill participants with core systemic theories, which transfers into relational social work practice. \r
\r
Lot 1 (B) Adults\r
\r
Within ASC most of our training courses run face to face and are to be held centrally at County Hall, Chelmsford. ESCA will organise and finance venues for the training to take place. \r
\r
Lot 2 - Strategic Leadership and Management \r
\r
The scope for the Strategic Leadership and Management programme is to deliver these courses with combined cohorts of Adult Social Care staff and Children and Families staff, commencing April 2025. \r
\r
This course is to be delivered face to face at County Hall, Chelmsford. ESCA will organise and finance venues for the training to take place. \r
\r
The target audience for this training course will be Directors, Service Managers and Aspiring Senior Managers. \r
\r
Providers are able to bid for both Lots, if they can meet the requirements set out in the Specification.

description:
Essex County Council (ECC) currently uses a Data Management System to manage and maintain the Greater Essex Dataset, which is a dataset of all bus routes (and associated timetables) for every legally registered local bus service in Essex, Southend and Thurrock. From this system, weekly uploads to data.essex.gov.uk are carried out in a variety of formats to support various in-house and external strategic planning data needs.\r

title: CO0410 Electric Bike Loan within the Workplace
description:
Essex County Council (ECC) is looking to commission an electric bike loan scheme targeted within the workplace. This scheme will support individuals facing travel and health inequalities within the work environment. \r
Essex Pedal Power, one of the flagship programmes of the Active Essex Local Delivery Pilot (LDP) is a scheme providing free bikes to residents in the county's most disadvantaged communities, to significantly increase cycling, active travel, and physical activity levels. Following the successes of Essex Pedal Power in Basildon, this project will run alongside and pilot the use of electric bikes to promote active travel to those facing perceived barriers to cycling, as well as individuals who are the most physically inactive. The Electric Bike Loan Scheme within the Workplace will contribute to outcomes set out by national organisations, such as the Department for Transport through Gear Change and Sport England in Uniting the Movement. Furthermore, it can be linked to commitments outlined in Everyone's Essex. We are looking for an electric bike subscription that will allow ECC to loan electric bikes to individuals free of charge, with a pilot of 50 bikes to at least 50 individuals over an initial 6-month pilot with the option to extend this further. This electric bike subscription should be inclusive of all costs including servicing, tyres, battery, motor, and any component failure due to wear and tear. \r

title: 1046 - Purchase of Containers Contract
description:
Essex is a large county with almost 1.5 million residents generating approximately 700,000 tonnes of local authority collected waste per annum. As the statutory Waste Disposal Authority for Essex, Essex County Council (the Authority) is responsible for providing a range of infrastructure and arrangements for the management of waste.\r
\r
The Authority operate 21 Recycling Centres for Household Waste (RCHW) and 4 Waste Transfer Stations (WTS), and work closely with the 12 borough, city and district councils who are the Waste Collection Authorities (WCA) within the county of Essex.\r
In April 2022, the Authority in-housed its waste service and therefore now operate and manage 21 Recycling Centres for Household Waste (RCHW) and 4 Waste Transfer Stations (WTS) across the County. \r
\r
The Authority are seeking to procure a contract for the provision of a quantity of up to twenty nine (29) new, forty (40) cubic yard open containers to enable the RCHW sites within the waste service to operate safely and compliantly.\r

title: Direct Payment Support Services Contract Award Notice
description:
Essex County Council ("the Council") conducted an open, single stage procurement to commission a new Direct Payments Support Service (DPSS) to enable people who are ordinarily resident within the administrative boundaries of Essex (excluding the unitary authority areas of Thurrock and Southend-on-Sea) to manage their direct payment.
This procurement incorporated the following lots:
Lot 1: Independent Information and Advice Service and Personal Assistant (PA) Support Hub
Lot 2: Payment/Payroll/Account Management services

title: PL0093 - Project THRIVE
description:
Project THRIVE - A research project that will investigate and evaluate a range of initiatives which aim to grow patronage on bus services.\r
\r
Essex County Council (ECC) has been allocated £4.9m in 2023/24 and £4.9m in 2024/25 from Department for Transport (DfT) Bus Service Improvement Plan Plus (BSIP+) funding, this BSIP+ funding will be used to support a range of initiatives that were set out in the Essex Bus Service Improvement Plan.\r
\r
The Thrive research project was originally set out in the Essex County Council Bus Service Improvement Plan 2021-2026 which was published in 2021. The aim of the Thrive research project is to explore what targeted measures may drive growth in market town bus services. This data led project will test a range of initiatives and assess which has the greatest impact on driving passenger growth.\r
\r
The initiatives delivered by suppliers identified through a multi-lot tender. The tendered project Lot's are: \r
\r
Marketing: Intense, traditional marketing campaign, including advertising, leaflet dropping and involvement of local councils to assist promotion (e.g. assist with promotion at transport hubs, tourist centres, etc).\r
\r
Digital Only Promotion: Digital and social media only promotion / marketing\r
\r
Better Information: Better information at bus stops along the route , through parishes, bus user groups, businesses, schools, clubs and communities.\r
\r
Increased frequency: Such as running the service every 30 minutes instead of hourly.\r
\r
ECC must ensure that all funding conditions under the BSIP+ Funding agreement are complied with - As defined in the BSIP Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) :\r
\r
3.2 The Authority may use the funding to target it on the actions that they - and local operators through their Enhanced Partnership (where relevant) - believe will deliver the best overall outcomes in growing long term patronage, revenues and thus maintaining service levels, whilst maintaining essential social and economic connectivity for local communities. In some places that may involve ensuring existing connections are maintained (either by conventional services or DRT). Elsewhere it might be achieved through increasing the frequency on key corridors or the operating hours of some services whilst reducing others; or reducing fares or introducing new local concessions to open up new markets and revenue.\r
\r
3.3 The funding must be spent on bus measures.\r
\r
3.6 The funding should not be used to support generic marketing or advertising costs that are not directly related to specific improvements (such as a fares change, or new services).\r
\r
ECC intend to utilise a minimal SSQ which will assess Potential Supplier Information and Exclusion Grounds.

title: EPP0129 - Bedding Plants
description:
Essex County Council, through the Essex Procurement Partnership, is procuring Bedding Plants on behalf of Tendring District Council.\r
\r
Tendring District Council ("the Council") places much emphasis on the quality of the environment within the District for the benefit of residents and visitors and the provision of high class and colourful bedding plant displays throughout its public gardens form a major part of current grounds maintenance programme.\r
\r
The Council uses a wide range of seasonal bedding plants in public gardens across the District, the main displays are located at Clacton Seafront, Crescent Gardens Frinton, Marine Gardens Walton and Mayors Garden Dovercourt. There are further smaller displays at other locations.\r
\r
Planting typically commences during the 1st week of June for Summer Bedding and the\r
1st week of October for Spring Bedding and is undertaken over three to four week periods. The Council's Open Spaces team carry out planting and maintenance across the District.\r
\r
Plants for spring bedding will be ordered by the end of May and plants for summer bedding will be ordered by the last week in October in each cyclic period. The Contractor will be advised of the exact planting dates for each planting period approximately one month before delivery, this will be dependent on growing conditions and how the current seasonal displays look.\r
\r
The contractor will be required to deliver all plants to nominated points throughout the District and timeliness of delivery is crucial. On average the Council orders approximately 45,000 to 67,500 plants per year for its displays approximately 40,000 to 60,000 for the summer period and 5,000 to 7,500 plants for the autumn period.\r
\r
The Council may order any combination of plants during the contract period for its bedding scheme The Council may place orders with the Supplier based upon a production list of plant requirements chosen from the Pricing Schedule, The pricing rate that shall be applied for each variety of each species will be determined by the total requirement for that variety contained within the individual order.\r
\r
For information there are no assets available for use on this contract. \r

title: Multiple and Complex Needs Service
description:
Essex County Council is seeking to commission a Multiple and Complex Needs Service to support individuals who are ordinarily resident within the administrative boundaries of Essex, excluding the unitary authority areas of Thurrock and Southend-On-Sea.\r
This procurement will ensure the continuation of the current Offenders with Additional and Complex Needs Service which is due to expire on 31st March 2024.  \r
\r
Since its inception in 2016 the current service has continued to evolve and has broadened to encompass therapeutic, holistic, wrap around intensive support which helps to stabilise and support individuals with multiple and complex needs. A key requirement of the Multiple and Complex Needs Service is first class relationship building with key local partners, ensuring multi and interagency collaboration with specialist treatment services and other partner providers.This tender will follow an open single stage process with a contract commencement date of 1 April 2024. \r
\r
The service will be commissioned under an initial five year term with the option of two extensions totalling not more than 48 months at the Council's sole discretion, thereby resulting in a maximum possible contract duration of nine years.\r
\r
The Council envisages that this procurement will be published on ProContract the week commencing Monday 10th July 2023. However, the Council reserves the right to postpone the publication in order to ensure suitable assurance that the tender documents are fit for purpose. Once the procurement is published a corresponding advertisement will be available via ProContract to enable prospective bidders to access, view and respond to this opportunity.\r

title: PH001 Reconnect - Early Help and Prevention
description: Essex County Council (ECC) is seeking to commission place-based, therapeutic interventions that support and encourage adults living with learning needs and/or disabilities, as well as those living with long term health conditions, to be physically active within their local area. Based on the learnings and insight from the Prevention and Enablement Model (PEM) pilot. The PEM Evaluation Report (which can be found here: https://www.activeessex.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/PEM-Evaluation-Report_FINAL.pdf) identified the need to scale the intervention across the 5 health alliance areas within Essex. The model(s) will focus on early help and prevention principles by offering bespoke support to identified adults, led jointly by an allied health professional and inclusive activity provider(s). We would look to commission a provider and/or consortium of providers to establish the model(s) within community leisure settings. The model(s) would include an allied health professional identifying the adults need or goals to help inform the most appropriate holistic intervention which can be supported via sport or physical activity. This could include but is not limited to swimming, sports games, cycling, dance, seated exercise or gym-based activities. The needs of an adult will differ but may include enhancing social skills and connections, strengthening motor or movement skills, building confidence and/or managing emotional wellbeing. The model requires co-designing interventions with the adults it aims to support, to ensure any activities are fully inclusive and accessible. Overall, the intention is for the model(s) to support adults' wellbeing and to support the building of confidence and connection to their community via physical activity opportunities.

title: Anti-Social Behaviour Pilots Monitoring and Evaluation Phase 2
description:
In March 2023 the government published the Anti-Social Behaviour Action Plan. Within this it committed £2.5m for a pilot for safer travel which builds on the model established in the West Midlands in 2021 and involves deployment of Transport Safety Officers (TSOs) on the transport network to enforce and help to reduce ASB. 
In November 2023 DfT announced that it will be funding four local authority areas to pilot TSOs on their transport network. They are: Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole; Lancashire County Council; Stoke-on-Trent City Council; and a consortium in Essex led by Thurrock Council in partnership with Southend-on-Sea City Council and Essex County Council. Pilots are expected to launch by end-January 2024 and conclude by March 2025. 
DfT is also providing funding to Transport for West Midlands to support delivery of the pilot programme, drawing on their experience of setting up the original TSO scheme, and to expand their TSO operation to incorporate a focus on Tackling Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG).
The evaluation aims to:
Understand the effectiveness of introducing Transport Safety Officers on local transport networks and the extent to which doing so reduces anti-social behaviour on public transport thereby making it safer for the public. 
Identify learn lessons and good practice that can be used to build capability across local government and enable other authorities to roll out similar interventions in their local areas. 
Inform future funding and operational decisions relating to deployment of Transport Safety Officers on local transport networks.
The evaluation programme will also feed into the department's work on tackling violence on women and girls on transport, providing valuable evidence about how elements of this intervention can contribute to delivery of specific actions specified in the Transport Champions Recommendations for Tacking Violence Against Women and Girls report and the wider ambition they are seeking to achieve.
Evidence from the evaluation will be used to respond to recommendations 11 and 12 in the Champions' report by providing evidence of the impact of having an increased presence of staff, including those with enforcement powers, on the transport network and the barriers and enablers to establishing effective partnerships between local authorities, police forces and transport operators

title: ESCC - RFQ - SME Energy Efficiency
description:
East Sussex County Council (the Council) provides a wide range of services on behalf of its residents, including social care, state education, roads, waste management, support to businesses and protection of the environment.

This requirement is for business support services within the Environment Team as part of the EU-funded Low Carbon Across the South and East 2 (LoCASE 2) program. LoCASE provides a business support program across the South East Local Enterprise Partnership (SELEP) area and helps businesses to adopt low carbon solutions in ways that improve business performance in terms of resilience, profitability and competitiveness, at the same time contributing to the protection and preservation of the environment.  LoCASE provides business support in the form of grants up to the value of £5,000 to increase demand for low carbon technology and to increase energy efficiency across the South East.
 
The LoCASE program has been funded by the European Regional Development Fund 2014-20. This project is receiving up to £7,138,387 of funding. The Department for Levelling Up, Communities and Housing is the Managing Authority for the European Regional Development Fund. 

The partners in this programme are Kent County Council, East Sussex County Council, Essex County Council, Southend-on-Sea Borough Council, Thurrock Council and the University of Brighton.

The Council procured a provider in 2020 to deliver part of LoCASE 2. We are looking for a new provider to take over and complete LoCASE 2 in East Sussex.

title: Independent Sexual Violence Advisors (ISVA) and Programme of Therapeutic Service
description:
Lot 1: Police and Crime Commissioner for Bedfordshire


The service commissioned will be to support all victims of rape and sexual violence abuse. The service will be an ISVA (Independent Sexual Violence Adviser) model of delivery, as the ISVA is a recognised, trained, and accredited professional role, there is a requirement for a mix of professionalism for children and adults. The service will also include a suite of therapeutic options to support victims to cope and recover from their experiences as far as feasible. 
It is anticipated that the contract will be let for a 3 years term with a potential extension of up to 2 years (1+1) thereafter , subject to good performance.


Lot 2: Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner for Essex in collaboration with Essex County Council

The service commissioned is to support victims of sexual abuse. This would be an all-age, all-gender service that offers help for victims regardless of the nature of the sexual abuse or when it happened. This would include child sexual abuse, child sexual exploitation, rape, and serious sexual assault (child and adult). The service would provide emotional and practical support as well as criminal justice support (through the provision of Independent Sexual Abuse Advisors (ISVAs), therapeutic support, counselling, and advocacy. The provision should give victims the support they need, be trauma informed, make victims feel safe, and improve feelings of resilience/empowerment.
It is anticipated that the contract will be let for a 3 years term with a potential extension of up to 4 years thereafter (2+1+1) , subject to good performance.

title: EPP0014 - Active Outdoor Gym
description:
Essex County Council are procuring on behalf of Tendring District Council an Active Outdoor Gym\r
\r
INTRODUCTION\r
Tendring District Council has secured £65,000 of funding to develop an active outdoor gym on land adjacent to York Road Car Park in Holland on Sea.\r
\r
Objectives\r
The purpose of the gym will be to improve strength and balance through natural, every day movement, and to offer rehabilitation in those recovering from injury or illness. The equipment must reflect that the community groups most likely to use this will be those with poorer mobility/dexterity. The colours used for equipment should reflect the fact that there may be users with forms of dementia, for which some colours can prove challenging.\r
The gym may be utilised by groups undertaking rehabilitation with a trained professional, or by members of the public alone. The layout of the equipment should facilitate this.\r
The Council is seeking to enter a contract with a suitably qualified contractor to install new equipment that will meet the objectives allowing for the best use of the funds within the available space.\r
The successful contractor will design and build the gym, including the surfacing and access, project managing the process from start to completion, as well as providing the required warranties and maintenance information.

title: CO0300 Leading Greater Essex
description:
Leading Greater Essex is a 12-month system leadership development programme, bespoke to the needs and ambitions of Greater Essex.  It brings together more than 65, emerging public and voluntary sector leaders each year to build a network of collaborative system leaders.\r
\r
Partners from across Greater Essex are sponsoring this programme together. The objective of the programme is to ensure 'whole system' thinking is embedded in public services across Essex, Southend and Thurrock.\r
\r
Essex Partners is made up of a number of Public Sector organisations including but not limited to Borough and District Councils, Voluntary sector organisations, blue light organisations, universities and NHS partners across Greater Essex.\r
\r
This Leadership Programme is underpinned by a shared Vision - The Future of Essex. The Future of Essex was designed by Essex Partners, with input from communities across the County, including: local people of all ages and backgrounds, community groups and schools; public, voluntary and private sector leaders, who have all contributed through interviews, surveys, engagement sessions, conversations and activities.\r
\r
The purpose of The Future of Essex is to give all the many, different communities, groups and businesses of Essex a way to collaborate in planning our future. To unite us. To set out the kind of Essex we want to live in. To transcend short-term agendas and move us towards the big things that matter to all of us. To take our pride in our county, and channel it for the good of everyone.\r

title: Economic and Employment Study Tender
description:
Tendring District Council and Colchester Borough Council in partnership with Essex County Council (the Councils) seek to appoint consultants to undertake an Economic and Employment Study to inform the preparation of the emerging Tendring Colchester Borders Garden Community Development Plan Document (DPD). The study will:
•	advise the Councils of the potential means of maximising the positive economic and employment generation opportunities of the Garden Community development
•	include analysis and options for location, format and potential end-users of the 25 hectares of employment allocation envisaged as part of the development
•	take into account the long-term nature of the development and the potential for innovation and change over the period of construction 
•	consider the wider objectives of the Garden Community, including the Garden Community Principles and the aspirations to create one new job per household, promote innovation and quality, achieve considerable 'modal shift' in favour of sustainable transport solutions and the need to create a vibrant local economy based on realistic market principles

title: Skills Bootcamps DPS : Education & Childcare : Second call off competition
description:
Skills Bootcamps offer flexible, primarily level 3 - 5 equivalent courses of up to 16 weeks in technical skills which are free to eligible adult learners. They give adults the opportunity to build up in-demand, sector-specific skills and fast-track to an interview with an employer - supporting adults to move into well-paid jobs and helping employers to fill much-needed vacancies. Unemployed, employed and self-employed adults can be eligible for a Skills Bootcamp; they can be used to support an unemployed person into a job, an employed adult into a different job in another organisation or to gain another role or other responsibilities in the same organisation, or a self-employed adult to gain new opportunities. They also support groups such as those returning to work after a break, ex-veterans and eligible prisoners within 6 months of release. There is a clear expectation that employers are involved in the whole end-to-end delivery of Skills Bootcamps; and where an employer is using a Skills Bootcamp to train up a current employee, they must contribute towards the costs of the Skills Bootcamp.
The Dynamic Purchasing System was launched in November 2022. This Contract Award Notice is for the contracts awarded under the Education and Childcare category.

title: CO0299 Multiply - Lot 3 - November 2023
description:
The purpose of this competition for Lot 3 "Helping people to manage their money and build confidence with maths" is to invite bids to create and deliver training provision for Essex residents who want to increase their numeracy skills in order to improve their ability to deal with everyday life challenges. These could include, but are not limited to, household budgeting, debt management, shopping and price comparison, food preparation, driving and travelling, DIY and home decorating, etc.

The provision could be offered as stand-alone modules or bolted on to existing (vocational) courses or support. 

Eligible target learners are adults 19+ who have not previously attained a GCSE Grade 4/C or higher maths qualification. 

We would be interested in opportunities that are developed in partnership with community organisations and other partners in Essex and aimed at engaging hardest-to-reach groups, e.g. unemployed or economically inactive people, people on low incomes, care leavers, people who are in or have recently been released from prison.

Expected duration of training courses is between 6 to 10 guided learning hours. 

Substantive learning (formal or informal) is defined as learning being delivered in two or more hours. All substantive learning will be recorded in the Individualised Learner Record (ILR) monthly. Suppliers will need to submit the ILR directly to the Department for Education via IDAMS. Where a supplier is unable to use IDAMS, it should submit via the ILR input tool. Suppliers will need to provide ECC with a copy of the ILR using an ECC template.

Department for Education (DfE) has confirmed that Multiply training / learning will not be subject to Ofsted inspections in Year 2 (2023-2024).

Outreach activities (a.k.a. non-substantive learning) should not be recorded in the ILR. title: CO0299 Multiply - Lot 3 - January 2024
description:
The purpose of this competition for Lot 3 "Helping people to manage their money and build confidence with maths" is to invite bids to create and deliver training provision for Essex residents who want to increase their numeracy skills in order to improve their ability to deal with everyday life challenges. These could include, but are not limited to, household budgeting, debt management, shopping and price comparison, food preparation, driving and travelling, DIY and home decorating, etc.

The provision could be offered as stand-alone modules or bolted on to existing (vocational) courses or support. 

Eligible target learners are adults 19+ who have not previously attained a GCSE Grade 4/C or higher maths qualification. 

We would be interested in opportunities that are developed in partnership with community organisations and other partners in Essex and aimed at engaging hardest-to-reach groups, e.g. unemployed or economically inactive people, people on low incomes, care leavers, people who are in or have recently been released from prison.

Expected duration of training courses is between 6 to 10 guided learning hours. 

Substantive learning (formal or informal) is defined as learning being delivered in two or more hours. All substantive learning will be recorded in the Individualised Learner Record (ILR) monthly. Suppliers will need to submit the ILR directly to the Department for Education via IDAMS. Where a supplier is unable to use IDAMS, it should submit via the ILR input tool. Suppliers will need to provide ECC with a copy of the ILR using an ECC template.

Department for Education (DfE) has confirmed that Multiply training / learning will not be subject to Ofsted inspections in Year 2 (2023-2024).

title: CO0348 Compostable Caddy Liners
description:
In Essex, food waste currently makes up around 26% of rubbish in a household's general waste bin. Minimising this level will deliver cost savings from avoided disposal and will reduce the environmental impact of food waste recycled by the kerbside food waste recycling collections by at least 10% in participating areas. The Customer will work in partnership with up to nine Waste Collection Authorities (WCAs) in Essex to support the roll-out of the Food Waste Recycling project.

The project's main activity will consist of a one-off delivery of a roll of compostable food caddy liners, an information leaflet, and a 'no food waste' bin sticker to suitable households across Essex. 

The Customer requires three separate deliveries of compostable food caddy liners to be delivered to a distribution company in accordance with each phase of the project: June 2023, September 2023 and January 2024.

title: Family Innovation Fund (2023-2026) - Brief Solution Focused Support
description:
The Family Innovation Fund enables ECC to work with its partners in the voluntary and community sector to deliver good outcomes as early as possible. The services will not support those children, young people and families already known to and in receipt of support from specialist and statutory services, rather they will ensure delivery of support that complements, not duplicates existing services such as;

• School funded support at additional levels of need
• Essex Child and Family Wellbeing Service
• Essex Integrated Wellbeing Service
• Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service
• Family Solutions

By Early Intervention we mean stopping something occurring or getting worse and for the purposes of this funding will provide brief, light touch interventions that will enable children, young people, parents and carers to draw on their own resources and resilience to resolve future problems.

This Grant is concerned with working with children and young people, parents/carers and families who will benefit from receiving support by way of Brief Solution Focussed Support (BSFS) such as coaching, mediation, conflict, through 1:1, group and family/parent/couples work. This will usually take place in face to face however, it may also take place using on-line platforms if that is deemed appropriate, for example during holiday periods or weekends/evenings.

title: ENCTS Administrative Services
description:
As a Transport Concession Authority (TCA), ECC has a statutory duty to provide qualifying residents with free bus passes under the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme (ENCTS). For the purposes of the ENCTS, qualifying residents are those persons who have either reached pensionable age or have a disability which qualifies them under legislation. 

This Scheme helps older people and people with disabilities live independently, those without other means of travel access work, health and shopping and by substituting for car journeys helps improve air quality, lowers carbon emissions and congestion.

Managing the scheme is a large scale and technical process, catering to more than 260,000, pass holders across Essex.

The Authority has entered into a Contract with a single Contractor, to provide administrative services to deliver this Scheme on our behalf, including the management of bus pass applications, assessments, data management, card production, customer contact, the reimbursement of bus operators and specialist consultant functions for the scheme. 

This Contract commences on the 1st April 2026, for an initial term of 2 years, with two 12-month extension provisions to be exercised at the Authority's sole discretion.

The value is anticipated to be £743,390 for the initial 2 year term; and should both the extension provisions be exercised, a total value of £1,449,114 for the 4 years.

title: CO0299 Multiply - Lot 4 - August 2023
description:
The purpose of this competition for Lot 4 "Full qualifications" is to invite bids to create and deliver new intensive and flexible Maths Functional Skills Qualification courses targeted at adults 19+ who have not previously attained a GCSE Grade 4/C or Level 2 maths qualification. 

In line with the Department for Education definition, Functional Skills qualifications should enable the learner to develop confidence in using mathematics and provide a foundation for progression into employment or further technical education and develop skills for everyday life, where the skills gained can be applied to solve mathematical problems. The purpose of Level 1 and Level 2 Functional Skills Mathematics qualifications is to demonstrate a sound grasp of mathematical skills at the appropriate level and the ability to apply mathematical thinking effectively to solve problems successfully in the workplace and in other real-life situations. 

Experience shows that skills providers in general commit 100% of their adult education budget in the Autumn term or risk reductions in subsequent years. ECC will encourage successful bidders to link with other Multiply providers from other Lots over time to encourage bite size learners from other Lots to progress to full qualifications throughout the year, particularly outside of the Autumn term. 

Multiply in Essex is keen to fund additional Maths Functional Skills Qualifications at NVQ 1 and NVQ 2 under this Lot. This aims to help adults to progress in learning and employment.   

Consideration would be given to funding additional Maths Functional Skills Qualifications at Entry Levels 1, 2 and 3, although bidders would need to provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate how these courses would generate exceptional impact and align with Multiply outcomes.

Functional Skills Qualifications should be accredited by a recognised national awarding body.  To avoid duplication with Adult Education Budget (AEB) funding qualifications, these should begin throughout the academic year, rather than at the standard September start.  

Expected duration of training courses is up to 55 guided learning hours. 
 
Learners will be expected to sit an examination at the end of the course to quantify their learning and provide them with certification as proof of their new skills. 

Examinations should be administered and certification awarded by a recognised, independent, national awarding body; the cost of which should be covered by the grant funding applied for.

title: CO0299 Multiply - Lot 3 - August 2023
description:
The purpose of this competition for Lot 3 "Helping people to manage their money and build confidence with maths" is to invite bids to create and deliver training provision for Essex residents who want to increase their numeracy skills in order to improve their ability to deal with everyday life challenges. These could include, but are not limited to, household budgeting, debt management, shopping and price comparison, food preparation, driving and travelling, DIY and home decorating, etc.

The provision could be offered as stand-alone modules or bolted on to existing (vocational) courses or support. 

Eligible target learners are adults 19+ who have not previously attained a GCSE Grade 4/C or higher maths qualification. 

We would be interested in opportunities that are developed in partnership with community organisations and other partners and aimed at engaging hardest-to-reach groups, e.g. unemployed or economically inactive people, people on low incomes, care leavers, people who are in or have recently been released from prison.

Expected duration of training courses is between 6 to 10 guided learning hours. 

Only substantive learning will be accepted for this tender and will be recorded in the Individualised Learner Record (ILR). Substantive learning (formal or informal) is learning being delivered in two or more hours.

Department for Education (DfE) has confirmed that Multiply training / learning will not be subject to Ofsted inspections in Year 2 (2023-2024).

Outreach activities (a.k.a. non-substantive learning) should not be recorded in the ILR. Instead, contact details (name, address, email, phone number & date of birth) should be collected from those engaged to enable follow up and marketing at a later date.

title: CO0299 Multiply - Lot 2 - August 2023
description:
The purpose of this competition for Lot 2 "Family Learning - supporting parents with children's schoolwork" is to invite bids to create and deliver training provision for parents wanting to increase their numeracy skills in order to help their children with schoolwork, and also help with their own progression. Working in schools, nurseries and community settings, we would like to enhance and scale up the family learning offer in Essex, whilst providing opportunities for parents to learn some valuable skills for life too.

Eligible target learners are parents and carers 19+ who have not previously attained a GCSE Grade 4/C or higher maths qualification and would like to enhance their knowledge. Learners will also have the opportunity to specifically learn how to support their child's/children's learning in the broader subject area of Maths. 

It is the intention that the provision will be delivered in locations that are convenient and easily accessible for learners, such as schools, nurseries and community settings. Bidders will ensure that this is a safe and appropriate learning environment.

Learning sessions will enable skills sharing through creative intergenerational interactions and reflective learning and encourage increased understanding between individuals of different age groups.

The learning experience will be further beneficial to parents and carers who will be able to acquire valuable life skills and improve their ability to deal with everyday life challenges such as household budgeting, debt management, shopping and price comparison, food preparation, etc.

Expected duration of training courses is between 6 to 10 guided learning hours.
 
Substantive learning (formal or informal) is learning being delivered in two or more hours. Only substantive learning will be accepted for this tender and will be recorded in the Individualised Learner Record (ILR). 

Department for Education (DfE) has confirmed that Multiply training / learning will not be subject to Ofsted inspections in Year 2 (2023-2024).

Outreach activities (a.k.a. non-substantive learning) should not be recorded in the ILR. Instead, contact details (name, address, email, phone number & date of birth) should be collected from those engaged to enable follow up and marketing at a later date.

title: EPP0114 - Clare Road Play Area
description:
Braintree District Council welcomes interested parties to participate in this tender for the 
refurbishment of the Clare Road Play Area. This project, funded under Section 106 (S106), 
aims to enhance the recreational facilities within our community whilst adhering to the 
highest safety standards.
Located at pods.forkful.blog (What Three Words location), the Clare Road Play Area requires 
comprehensive revitalisation to ensure it remains a vibrant hub for children and families alike. 
As part of this endeavour, the Council has outlined a detailed specification that encompasses 
the replacement and enhancement of existing play equipment across both open field areas 
and the toddler (fenced) play area.
In line with Framework Agreement PROC20-0107, prospective bidders are invited to submit 
proposals for various aspects of the refurbishment project. This includes the removal and 
replacement of outdated equipment with new installations designed to promote inclusive and 
engaging play experiences.
Crucially, all proposed works must meet stringent safety requirements, with particular 
attention paid to overlaying wet pour safety surfaces and creating no-edge surfaces to 
mitigate potential hazards. Additionally, post-installation inspections are integral to this 
tender, ensuring the ongoing safety and longevity of the refurbished play areas.
The scope of work spans from the removal and replacement of swing bays and inclusive 
roundabouts to the revitalisation of trim trails and toddler play equipment. Furthermore, 
measures such as weed control and surface overlay are essential components to be addressed 
within the tender proposals.
Braintree District Council invites capable and experienced contractors to submit 
comprehensive bids that align with the outlined specifications. Through collaborative efforts, 
we aim to rejuvenate the Clare Road Play Area, providing a safe, inclusive, and enjoyable 
environment for generations to come.
Prospective bidders are encouraged to carefully review the provided specifications and submit 
their proposals by the designated deadline. Should you require any further clarification or 
information, please do not hesitate to contact the Council's procurement team.
This tender has a maximum budget of £82,666.10.

title: C005PC  St Botolph's Circus
description:
The scheme comprises significant public realm improvements to the existing St Botolph's Circus in Colchester, and associated highway works, including new at-grade crossings for active travel models and the removal from use of the existing three subways / underpasses, referred to as the Proposed Scheme.
St Botolph's Circus is located to the south of Colchester city centre at the junction of Southway (A134) to the west, Magdalen Street (A134) to the east, Mersea Road (B1025) to the south, and St Botolph's Street to the north.

The site functions as a large 'gateway' junction, leading to the city centre. The Future Transport Strategy defines the St Botolph's Circus area as both Zone 1 (city centre) and Zone 4 (Strategic Transport Corridor).

The Proposed Scheme aims to:
• Create a good quality urban realm and gateway to the city centre.
• Develop an improved, safer environment for everyone.
• Improve connectivity for communities to local and wider transport networks through bus, rapid transit and rail services and walking and cycling routes.
• Ensure an inclusive and accessible area for all.
• Balance the requirements of different travel modes
• Reduce anti-social behaviour and the fear of crime.
• Improve health and wellbeing for Colchester residents.
• Increase footfall to encourage wider economic growth of the area, provide development opportunities and support local business.

The key elements of the scheme are:

• New public realm area to the north east and north west areas of the Circus, with high quality paving, new planting, landscaping and seating.
• New at-grade traffic signal-controlled crossings on all four arms of the Circus for active travel modes.
• New footways and cycleways, including a link on the north side of Southway between the Circus and Whitwell Road.
• Partial filling-in of the existing roundabout and subways / underpasses, including installing pipes in the existing subways for new drainage attenuation.
• A new retaining wall on the south-western corner to enable carriageway widening and associated earthworks.
• Improved bus stop facilities at the Mersea Road (southbound) stop.
• Carriageway widening, reconstruction and surfacing.
• Enhanced lining and traffic signal installations.
• Surface water drainage works.
• Kerbing, footway construction / reconstruction and landscaping including some tree replacement, planting new trees, wildflower planting.
• Signage works and street furniture.
• Street lighting replacement and upgrades.

title: Provision of a flexible &apos;Cafeteria&apos; style contract for Continuing Health Care Services in Mid and South Essex
description:
The Authority has awarded a contract for the provision of a &apos;cafeteria style contract&apos;, which for the purposes of this procurement means "a zero guarantee, activity based contract for the delivery of a comprehensive range of AACC support services, allowing the Essex ICB to flexibly call off any volume or type of CHC assessment or review activity as required, without committing to minimum volumes or fixed activity guarantees) to Carehome Selection Limited trading as Xyla, using a Compliant Framework procedure The Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust - National Framework Agreement for All Age Continuing Care Services dated 4th December 2023 with Framework Agreement reference F/092/ACCSS/23/MH under the Public Contract Regulations 2015.

The Contract will be for a term of 12 months from 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2027 (with a potential extension of a further 12 months until 31st March 2028).. The Authority provided for a potential extension of up to 12 months until 31st March 2028 to future proof this contract, but this is in no way guaranteed, and activation of such extension will be at the sole discretion of the Authority based on fundamental principles laid out in the Tender Documents, as well as the performance of the provider and results of any service evaluations undertaken.

NHS Mid and South Essex ICB currently has insufficient workforce and capacity within its NHS CHC function therefore requires support in delivery of CHC Services to meet its statutory requirements. NHS Mid and South Essex ICB require this support to be on a flexible basis i.e. ability to call-off variable volume and type of support in line with capacity and demand.

The CHC Services includes:
- CHC Reviews (CHC/Funded Nursing Care/Fast Track)
- CHC Assessments
- CHC Retrospective reviews of Previously Unassessed Periods of Care (PUPoC)
- CHC Appeals.

On 1 April 2026, NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board will cease to exist and will be replaced by NHS Essex Integrated Care Board (comprised of Mid and South Essex in full, West Essex from current NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB, and North East Essex from NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB).

NHS Essex ICB will hold the statutory responsibility for the delivery of All Age Continuing Healthcare (AACC) - comprised of NHS Continuing Healthcare (CHC), and Children and Young Peoples Continuing Care (CYPCC) - across Essex. Therefore, NHS Essex ICB will have a continued requirement for this support following transition on the 1 April 2026. The proposed contract, alongside moving to new Operating Model, will provide the ICB with sufficient workforce capacity to cover all areas of AACC delivery.

The indicative value for the service is £1,904,544 (exclusive of VAT) and £2,285,452 (inclusive of VAT) for the initial 12 months of the contract. If the extension is enacted the cumulative indicative value would be £3,809,088 (exclusive of VAT) and £4,570,905 (inclusive of VAT).

title: Children & Young People Therapeutic Health Based Coaching - NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board (Essex wide)
description:
This Contract Award notice follows the publication of a Voluntary Ex-Ante Transparency Notice, published on 17.04.2023 (Notice reference: 2023/S 000-010912), the purpose of which was intended to provide notice of the NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB), NHS Mid and South Essex ICB and Suffolk and NHS North East Essex ICB&apos;s (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") intention to award a contract for Therapeutic Health Based Coaching Services under Regulation 32 (2) (a), to the incumbent provider N.O.W&apos;s The Time For Change, for a period of 12 months from 1st May 2023 to 30th April 2024, at an aggregate contract value of £406,800 (excluding VAT). Prior to conclusion of the contract, The Authority applied a voluntary 10-day standstill period from the publication of the VEAT.

The Therapeutic Health Based Coaching Service will deliver support to parents and carers of children
and young people who live in Essex and who have been in contact with the Southend, Essex and
Thurrock Children&apos;s and Adolescent Mental Health Service (SET CAMHS) and are receiving treatment. The
service will also act as an additional support element for families who are experiencing anxiety,
depression or require support in their current situation.

The key outcomes of the service are to:

- Provide therapeutic support to families who are facing the additional challenges of emotional wellbeing,
anxiety, low mood etc. affecting a child or young person;
- Encourage communication between family members
- Explore any fears, anxieties, difficulty or distress
- Help with conflict and conflict resolution skills
- Help reduce feelings of isolation
- Identify and facilitate ways to address contributing factors in their daily lives
- Gain insight into, and explore strategies to improve, their situation
- Find practical solutions to the daily challenges

The Authority issued a Contract Notice (2023/S 000-003382) communicating to the market that the
Authority was commencing a competitive procurement for the provision of Therapeutic Health Based
Coaching Service, on 3rd February 2023. A Light Touch Open Procedure was completed by the Authority
in accordance with such Contract Notice, however on this occasion there were unfortunately no suitable
tenders submitted in response to this procedure, and the procedure was abandoned.

Based on positive outcomes for and feedback regarding the pilot, the Authority wishes to ensure
continuity of provision of the Service to Children and Young People and their Parents and Carers across
Essex. As such the Authority has taken a decision to continue to work with the incumbent provider for
another 12 months to provide sufficient time to deliver a second procurement process, details of which
will be communicated to the market in due course via relevant Contract Notices.

title: Children & Young People Crisis Support Service - Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB (Essex-wide)
description:

Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board (HWE ICB) has awarded a contract to deliver a Children
& Young People&apos;s Crisis Support Service across Southend, Essex and Thurrock.

This service is being commissioned by Herts and West Essex ICB as the lead commissioner on behalf of the county and in conjunction with Mid & South Essex integrated Care Board and Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board as associate commissioners.

The Crisis Support Service provides therapeutic support, based on the provision such as the trauma
informed attachment focussed therapy model, as an example. This will enable parents and carers to adopt
and maintain a therapeutic parenting approach.

The key outcomes of the service are to:

- Alleviate the stress of social isolation, concerns about managing a CYP with emotional, anxiety or other

title: Locally Enhanced Services for Thurrock Alliance (NHS Mid and South Essex ICB)
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Authority, South East Essex Alliance on behalf of NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs). This Contract Award is made by the Authority to the 27 General Practitioner (GP) providers within the south east Essex (previously Castle Point and Rochford and Southend areas) geographical footprint for the provision of Locally Enhanced Services (LES).

The provision of Locally Enhanced Services to include:
- 24 Hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring
- Gonadorelin Analogue Injections
- Minor Injury Services
- Phlebotomy
- Secondary & Community Care Wound Management Services
- Non Scalpel Vasectomy Service (NSV)
- 24 Hour Electrocardiogram
- Shared Care
- Anticoagulation (Warfarin)

The Authority has taken the decision to award this Locally Enhanced Service (which was previously commissioned for NHS Castle Point and Rochford CCG and Southend CCG) to the 47incumbent General Practitioner (GP) providers. As of July 2022, the Integrated Care Board (ICB) superseded the previous 5 CCGs within Mid and South Essex. NHS Mid and South Essex ICB is currently undergoing an organisational restructure and have taken the decision to extend the current contract to the incumbent providers for 12 months whilst commissioning decisions and strategies can be made for the future of this service. The Authority considers these 47 GP providers for this LES as technically capable of providing the most economically advantageous solution to the Authority whilst the ICB undergoes restructure, review and alignment of contracts. title: PDPS Voluntary Sector and SME Specialist Contracts Framework for NHS Mid and South Essex ICB
description:
This is contract award notice and intended to communicate that NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (NHS MSE ICB) is seeking to establish a Pseudo Dynamic Purchasing System (PDPS) framework provision for small and medium enterprises (SME)s, Voluntary Sector Charity Organisations (VSCOs), and organisations who could deliver purpose led services within the Mid and South Essex ICB localities.

As advertised within the previous Find a Tender Opportunity Advert (notice number 2023/S 000-037030), this PDPS framework will be for a 4-year period from 01/04/2024 - 31/03/2028.

Under this PDPS the Authority may look to award a Call-Off Contract of between a minimum of 3 and maximum 24 months to a provider who has been pre-approved and gained entry onto the Approved Provider List. The headline mechanisms for undertaking a Call Off Procedure under this PDPS are set out later in the procurement pack and will be detailed within each Call-Off Invitation to Tender (ITT). The Services to which this procurement relates above threshold of the Light Touch Regime of the Public Contract Regulations (PCR 2015) (as amended The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020).

In order to be accepted onto the PDPS, all Bidders responding to the Stage 1: Request to Participate will complete the mandatory Selection Questionnaire, Qualification and Technical envelopes within the e-procurement portal. The Authority aims to open the PDPS each year to allow for new providers to Request to Participate, complete the mandatory questionnaires and onboard onto the PDPS.

As advertised in this Find a Tender Opportunity Advert, this PDPS has no activity guarantee, with a minimum contract value of £0.00 per annum. Please note that the notice published in a Find a Tender notice has reflected a minimum value of £1.00 due to "cvc-minExclusive-valid: Value &apos;0.0&apos; is not facet-valid with respect to minExclusive &apos;0.0&apos; for type &apos;cost&apos;." error which prevents the true figure of £0.00 per annum being illustrated. The maximum indicative aggregate contract value £500million. This indicative value was calculated by using the Authority&apos;s actual annual spend across a wide range of voluntary, small and medium-sized enterprises, specialist and locality specific purpose led services across the entire geography of Mid and South Essex. The Authority aims to procure such services via this PDPS (once it is established). Any services that do not align with the aims and objectives of this PDPS will be procured outside of this PDPS, in strict accordance with the Regulations.

This procurement commenced before the 01st January 2024 and therefore the Health and Care Act 2022 and the new regime. For absolute clarity, the Provider Selection Regime (PSR) does not apply to this specific contract award for this "Round 1" of the PDPS Framework. All new opportunities or "Rounds" will be appropriately advertised on the Find a Tender Service platform and will be in accordance with the PSR.

description:
Southend-on-Sea City Council is undertaking a procurement for a LoRaWAN IOT Network across South Essex via CCS RM6116 Network Services 3 Lot 3a IoT and Smart Cities (Smart shared and connected spaces) on behalf of ASELA (Association of South Essex Local Authorities).

ASELA has secured funding from Highways England to design, build and deliver a LoRaWAN IOT Network across South Essex.

The procurement will be to:
• Deliver contiguous outdoor coverage across the South Essex.
• Design, build and manage a network that will be owned by ASELA'S Local Authority Partners.
• Deliver a LoRaWAN IOT network driven by outcomes specified by the ASELA partners.
• Create an Open and "Free to use an outdoor " LoRaWAN Network connected into the Things Network which should also incorporate a capability to deliver a future Carrier Class solution. This Dual network requirement capability must be built within the Gateway hardware deployed to support your bid solution.
• Deliver a network that will provide support for multiple sensors (types / manufactures) and solutions, but still be integrated in respect to collecting and sharing data. There should not be additional costs to add sensors to the "Free to Use" network.
• Support through access to open data work with schools and empower local digital skill training.
• Provide data to inform public sector policy and strategy
• Support the delivery of future public services.
• Stimulate innovation and economic growth to enable local businesses to embrace the opportunities offered by IOT and to grow accordingly.
• Secure a delivery partner who is willing to partner and develop the opportunities offered by this LoRaWAN network and be innovative around approach to delivery and cost models.

title: ASD Post-Diagnostic Psychoeducational Resource for Parents/Carers and Young People in Greater Essex
description:
The Contracting Authority(s) (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") for this Due Diligence are NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB), NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB and NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB.

The Authority has awarded a contract to KIDS for the design, development, digitisation and pilot implementation of two psychoeducational resources, across Essex, Southend, and Thurrock. These will be evidence-based therapeutic interventions, that provide information and support to better understand and cope with autism for CYP and for parents and carers of CYP, following diagnosis.

The project aims to deliver the national and local ambition to design and implement a psychoeducational resource which:

- Provides information about autism as a diagnosis.
- Helps people come to terms with their diagnosis.
- Identifies additional coping strategies for everyday challenges (such as managing difficult sensory environments or stigma).
-Provides opportunities to engage with other autistic people who may have had similar experiences.
-Helps the parent/carer or young person feel empowered in living with their diagnosis.

The content will be evidence based, co-produced with families and professionals, and include a range of topics including financial advice, relational peer support, relationship management, emotional adjustment, long term stress management, resilience, stigma protection etc.

Successful delivery will require a combination of expertise, skills and experience in terms of the digital sphere, alongside experience of working with children, young people and families with SEND.

title: North Essex Heritage - Jumbo Water Tower - Business Planner and Development Appraisal Procurement - AWARD
description:
Colchester's Balkerne Water Tower, affectionately known as 'Jumbo', is the largest Victorian municipal water tower in England. Completed in 1883, it is grade II* listed, and maintained its original use until 1984. It has local significance as a beacon of Colchester standing tall on the skyline, and national significance as the last remaining listed water tower still intact, a testament to the feat of Victorian engineering that brought a public water supply to the masses.
      
      Colchester and North East Essex Building Preservation Trust's (North Essex Heritage) mission is to save Jumbo from dereliction and see it removed from the Buildings At Risk register, producing a commercially viable operation that opens access to the public allowing all to appreciate the engineering marvel and superb views. It will bring the magnificent Balkerne Water Tower back into use, creatively converting it to provide a fully accessible heritage visitor attraction for the city, combined with complementary commercial uses to add to revenue to achieve financial sustainability for the long-term future.
      
      The project has been successful in securing Development funding from the Towns Deal and NLHF Heritage Enterprise scheme.  This funding is to be used to prove the viability of the project, and provide confidence in the ability of the Trust and partners to deliver this project.
      
      North Essex Heritage is now seeking to separately appoint the following roles to support the development of the project:
      
      - A Business Planner to work with the Trust to explore the operational model and business plan for Jumbo, preparing a NLHF compliant Business Plan for Round Two submission, and remaining with the project through Delivery and into Operation to provide guidance and updates to the Business Plan so it remains a live working document.  Total life of contract anticipated to be a 5 year period.  Total value of commission is in the region of £40,000.
      - Development Appraisal that meets the requirements of the NLHF Heritage Enterprise funding regime, undertaking the valuation of the building and calculating the conservation deficit, as well as working with the Business Planner to establish the viability of different operating models.  Appointment will be for 9 months and value of commission is £15,000.

title: Primary Care Post op Cataract Service
description:
This notice is to provide confirmation of the award of a contract to Primary Eyecare Services Ltd by NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board.  This service will be delivered in the West Essex &apos;place&apos; area only and does not cover the whole of the Hertfordshire and West Essex.

The Post-Op Cataract Service (POCS) is a service which manages Optometrists undertaking cataract follow-ups in the community, rather than within the Acute or Independent Sector.  This contract award follows a very low value pilot contract (£5,150 excl. VAT) which ran between April 2022 to March 2023 and was extended until 30th September 2023.

The evaluation of the pilot demonstrated that the service had met the agreed outcomes and KPIs moving follow up activity away from the acutes and into the community which achieved a better experience for patients through streamlining the pathways and at a lower cost.

Primary Eyecare Services is a non-profit organisation of the Essex Local Ophthalmology Community (LOC).  This means that the local ophthalmologists who would deliver this service are within the trade body of the Essex LOC.  This model brings the additional benefits of expert clinical knowledge, advice and can assist with service commissioning and delivery.  The pathway requires engagement with local optometrists and is crucial to delivering a community pathway which is achievable through the Essex LOC rather than contracting with local optometrists individually which may introduce fragmentation and risk achievement of the positive outcomes for patients.

The contract will start on 1st October 2023 and will end on 31st March 2025 with the option to extend for a further 12 months to 31st March 2026.

The value identified in this waiver is the total cumulative value inclusive of the option to extend and inclusive of VAT.  The total value of the initial contract duration is £107,700 (exclusive of VAT.  Inclusive of VAT this is £129,240).

As this was an under threshold non-competitive award, the closing date identified in this Notice is the date on which the waiver was approved through ICB internal governance.

title: Essex All-Age Autism Outreach Service
description:
This notice is intended to provide confirmation of an awarded contract for an Essex All-Age Autism Outreach Service providing specialist autism support to autistic individuals of all ages, across the Transforming Care Partnership (TCP) footprint of Southend, Essex and Thurrock (SET).

The contract is for 4 years from 1st May 2024 to 30th April 2028, with an option to extend for a further two years until 30th April 2030.

The value of this 4-year contract is ££4,769,000.This will increase to £8,153,500 if the option to extend is utilised. Both values are exclusive of VAT.

The Authority invited suitably qualified service providers to submit tenders for the provision of an Essex All-Age Autism Outreach Service across the East of England Region.

The Service will aim to achieve the ambitions of Building the Right Support and the NHS Long Term Plan by reducing the number of avoidable admissions of autistic people to tier 4 and inpatient services and improving the quality of life and care of autistic people in both inpatient services and the community. 

It will consist of a 'core offer' for Children, Young People and Adults as well as crisis offer for Children and Young People.

The service will be expected to work with individuals, across a variety of settings, as well as supporting their families and offering consultation to other professionals/services to support the understanding of the individual's needs 'through an autism lens'. The service will also be expected to offer hands on, practical support to implement its recommendations, with a more intensive offer of this support for children and young people forming a 'crisis offer'. Engagement with individuals and their families tell us the importance of support being &apos;for autistic people, by autistic people', and there will be an expectation that lived experience is held at the centre of the service's offer and values, employing individuals with lived experience to enhance the support offered.

The type of support the service will be expected to provide includes:

Support with understanding and managing sensory processing issues

Providing adapted psychological therapies to meet the needs of the individuals accessing support (this may include art, play, music, and animal therapy)

Support individuals with understanding their identity (in relation to autism, neurodiversity, sexuality, and gender etc.)

Autism specialist strategies and skill development around issues such as, but not limited to, executive functioning, problem solving, communication, relationships, socialising, behaviour, and sleep. 

Peer to peer support (for individuals and their families) to offer advice and knowledge from a lived experience perspective.

Joint working with other teams/service to support the better understanding of an individual's needs 'through an autism lens'- this may include, but isn't limited to, CAMHS teams, adult mental health teams and eating disorder teams etc.
