description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Contracting Authority; Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs).

Following a nine-month extension from 1st July 2023 to 31st March 2024, , the Authority is seeking to further extend this service for an additional 12-month period from 1st April 2024 to 31st March 2025. 

The pilot undertaken within Primary Care, supported by non-recurrent Primary Care funding for 23/24, has undergone a full evaluation at the end of the pilot period, reviewing outcomes against need to determine future commissioning requirements. The initial outcome of the evaluation identified the need to secure ongoing provision of this service in response to General Practice needs. 

With increasing pressures being faced across local General Practice, further conversations have occurred over the last year within the Sustainability and Resilience Programme, through engagement with Primary Care and key system stakeholders like the LMC, to understand what is needed to best respond to challenges faced now and into the future, and secure continuing high-quality care for patients. 

This period of engagement has identified various interdependencies between existing commissioned services and further time is required to explore and understand the full impact of these interdependencies to inform future commissioning plans and the exact scope of service support offers required. 

In the interim, to support the ongoing response to challenges and inform the development of the General Practice Support Programme, we will extend the Wrap Around Support and Recovery Group for an additional 12 months. 

GP Primary Choice Ltd (GPPC) who have delivered the service during the pilot period, are an established organisation within North East Essex, with key relationships and links with Primary Care as well as knowledge obtained about the needs within practices from the previous pilot term. This places them in a unique position to deliver this extension in a way that will support the ongoing realisation of the maximum benefits possible within the 12 month pilot period, with minimal disruption to current service delivery, and no additional mobilisation requirements to inform future commissioning options.

The contract award is made to GPPC for the provision of Wrap Around Support and Recovery across Suffolk and North East Essex. 

The contract term is 12 months, commencing 1st April 2024 and expiring on 31st March 2025, at a total aggregate Contract Value of £66,712.30 (excl. VAT).

The Authority is publishing this Contract Award Notice in the Contracts Finder in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended by The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020) for spend above £30,000.

title: 1:1 in Care Homes Commissioning for Mid and South Essex
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Contracting Authority; NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs).

The contract award is made to 1 Stop Healthcare Staffing Ltd for the provision 1:1 Support in Care Homes across Mid and South Essex.

It was identified that 1:1 provision of care in nursing homes has an impact on both areas. Staff shortages in the care market, increase in activity due to winter pressures and providers finding it increasingly difficult to recruit staff, all impact on a nursing home being able to accept a patient requiring 1:1 support. Nursing Homes in Mid Essex have been invited to take part in the second phase of a pilot and to provide feedback on the proposed model of care. This will ensure that any concerns highlighted from the first phase and ahead of the second phase of the pilot launch can be identified and dealt with as required.

The contract term is 12 months, commencing 01/03/2023 and expiring on 31/03/2024, at a total aggregate Contract Value of £500,000.

title: Wrap Around Support and Recovery Group Service in Suffolk and North East Essex
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Contracting Authority; Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs).

Following a three-month extension from 1st April - 30th June 2023, the Authority, are seeking a further waiver to extend this service for an additional nine-month period from 1st July 2023 - 31st March 2024. 

The pilot undertaken within Primary Care, supported by non-recurrent Primary Care funding for 22/23, has undergone a full evaluation at the end of the pilot period, reviewing outcomes against need to determine future commissioning requirements. The initial outcome of the evaluation identified the need to secure ongoing provision of this service in response to General Practice needs. 

Over recent months, with increasing pressures being faced across local General Practice and the NEE Alliance, it has been highlighted that there is a need for a further review of commissioned General Practice resilience offers. To this end, funding has been allocated to a Resilience and Sustainability Programme in North East Essex to work in collaboration with system partners to create a local offer for General Practice which is fit for purpose to respond to challenges faced now and (as far as possible) into the future to secure continuing high quality care for patients.

The Sustainability and Resilience Programme will aim to deliver a menu of support that will be available to Practices to respond to challenges, and undertake quality improvement to support increased sustainability and resilience, ensuring Practice teams are best placed to respond to challenges faced now and into the future, and secure continuing high quality care for patients. 

The Authority recognise that they are unable to develop this offer in isolation and that the knowledge of what is needed to best support General Practice to increase sustainability and resilience sits within General Practice and General Practice support networks such as the Local Medical Committee. It is on this basis that the Authority will be setting out to engage with system partners to inform the development of this programme offer. 

The contract award is made to GP Primary Choice Ltd. for the provision of Wrap Around Support and Recovery across North East Essex. 

The contract term is 9 months, commencing 1st July 2023 and expiring on 31st March 2024, at a total aggregate Contract Value of £37,787.83 (excl. VAT).

title: Teledermatology Service for Suspected Cancer Referrals for Mid and South Essex
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Contracting Authority; NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs). 

The contract award is made to Skin Analytics for provision of Teledermatology Services for suspected cancer referrals across Mid and South Essex. The contract term is for 9 months, commencing 01st July 2022 and expiring on 31st March 2023, at a total aggregate Contract Value of £111,375.

The Service:
The service is currently used by 44 of the 150 GP Practices across the system, which is 29%. 

The skin analytics pathway is a pre-referral pathway service, which involves image capture of suspected cancerous lesions within primary care using an iPhone with dermatascope attachment, the lesion is then assessed by artificial intelligence whereby if suspicious this is returned to the GP/HCP instantly to be referred on a 2 wait week referral to secondary care. If lesion is suspected benign then this is reviewed by a Skin Analytics consultant Dermatologist and returned to the GP/HCP within two working days with referral action or advice. 

During the period April 21 - Feb 22 there were 13,853 2ww skin referrals into the Trust from GP practices across Mid and South Essex. During the period April 21 - March 22, Skin Analytics have undertaken 3,758 assessments with; 49% of patients (1,841) being recommended to be referred on a 2ww pathway, 10% (376) being recommended to be referred on a routine pathway to secondary care, 7% (263) being recommended to be treated within primary or community care with 29% (1,090) being discharged from primary care. The award is a short term, non recurrent award by the Authority for a total term of 9 months at an aggregate value of £111,375.00 Sterling.

The Authority is publishing this Contract Award Notice in the Contracts Finder in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended by The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020) for spend above £25,000. The Services in scope of this Contract Award Notice fall within &apos;social and other specific services&apos; within the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended by The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020), but the total contract value does not exceed the current threshold of £663,540.

title: Dynamic Support Register Keyworker Service
description:
Hereafter all references to the Authority incorporates: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB), NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB and NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB.

The Authority has awarded a contract for the Provision of a Pan Essex Dynamic Support Register Keyworker (non-clinical) Service (the Service) to HCRG Care Services Ltd, using an open procedure under the Public Contract Regulations 2015.

The Contract will be for a term of 36 months from 1st April 2025 until 31st March 2028. The Authority provided for a potential extension of up to 24 months until 31st March 2030 to future proof this contract, but this is in no way guaranteed, and activation of such extension will be at the sole discretion of the Authority based on fundamental principles laid out in the Tender Documents, as well as the performance of the provider and results of any service evaluations undertaken.

The Contract to be entered into by the Authority and the HCRG Care Services Ltd will be based on the NHS Terms and Conditions for the Provision of Services 2024/25 (version dated August 2022) and all subsequent variations thereof.

The aggregate value of the contract over the term (including extensions) as advertised in Find a Tender Service is £4,715,395 excluding VAT. The Contract Value for the three-year term, which acted as an affordability envelope for the purposes of bidding, is £2,829,147.

The Authority undertook an open tender to identify a suitably qualified and experienced and technically and professionally capable provider to deliver the Service for Children & Young People (CYP) with learning disabilities and/or autism (LD/A) up to the age of 25, within Southend, Essex & Thurrock (SET). Locally, SET have too many CYP with LD/A admitted to Tier 4 hospital settings according to national targets. Embedding the DSR Keyworker Service aims to reduce these admissions for those up to the age of 25 where avoidable and help to maintain and support the CYP&apos;s placement within the community.

The Authority has appointed a single Preferred Bidder to manage all aspects of the Service. As such, a Lotting Strategy was deemed inappropriate and not used, as it risked creation of unnecessary fragmentation and complexity. Accordingly, the service has been offered as a single contract awarded to a single Preferred Bidder (HCRG Care Services Ltd).

title: SC23237 - KEIFCA Cabin RIB
description:
The district of Kent & Essex Inshore Fisheries and Conservation Authority (K&EIFCA) contains some of the most attractive, productive and intensively used coastal waters in the UK; from the small picturesque harbours of Whitstable, Leigh and West Mersea to the major industrial ports of Harwich, London and Dover. This marine environment includes unique features such as the Essex mud flats and marshes, offshore sandbanks, the Kent chalk cliffs and cobble beaches all of which contain a fascinating array of habitats and species. K&EIFCA has been created to sustainably manage local inshore fisheries resources and protect this diverse marine environment.

Kent & Essex IFCA district covers an area of over 3,412 km2, and extends from the east end of Rye Bay in Kent to the northern boundary of Essex on the River Stour. The seaward boundary follows the coast to the 6-mile nautical limit measured from the 1983 baseline, which, due to drying sand banks, extends up to 15 miles offshore in some places. The up-river K&EIFCA boundary in the Thames includes the waters adjacent to Kent County Council and Thurrock Council, with the district boundary running from Dartford creek (River Darent) on the south shore to Mar Dyke on the North Shore. The other district limits for the rest of the rivers located within the boundaries of Kent and Essex extended to their tidal limit (including, the Medway, the Blackwater and the Colne).

The requirement was to build of a 9.5 - 11m cabin RIB subject to a tendering process. The size and enclosed protection of a cabin RIB provides an elevated and protected vantage point, enhancing surveillance capabilities over those provided by existing vessels to monitor larger areas of the water and detect potential illegal fishing activities effectively. Whilst the cabin would allow for extended patrols, enabling officers to stay on the water for longer durations, ensuring continuous presence in critical areas.

title: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB Translation Services - Primary Care
description:
The Contracting Authority (NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board) has awarded a Call-Off Contract for provision of a Translation Services - Primary Care in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (which are the regulations under which the Framework Agreement was established prior to Procurement Act 2023 coming into force (24th Feb 2025)), using via a compliant Call-Off under the NHS North of England Commercial Procurement Collaborative - Language Services Framework Agreement (NOE.0583) under Lot 1A - Managed Services. 
 
As a result of the evaluation undertaken in accordance with the Framework Guidance and Rules, Language Empire Ltd - was selected as Preferred Bidder for provision of Language Services Lot 1A Managed Service - All other regions, specifically for Primary Care within Mid and South Essex.  The scope of this service includes: 
 
- Face to Face Interpretation Services - Spoken 
- Face to Face Interpretation Services - Non-Spoken 
- Telephone Interpretation Services 
- Video Interpretation Services - Spoken 
- Video Interpretation Services - Non-Spoken 
- Translation, Transcription and Additional Services 
 
The contract commences 01st November 2025 and expires 31st October 2028. The aggregate contract value awarded is £335,112 by Will (£111,704 per annum).  
 
The Procurement Act guidance (Guidance: transitional and saving arrangements (HTML) - GOV.UK) states that any contracts awarded through a framework agreement under the previous legislation will continue to be managed in accordance with that legislation. As such, this call-off contract awarded under NHS North of England Commercial Procurement Collaborative - Language Services Framework Agreement (NOE.0583) under Lot 1A - Managed Services. that was established on 02/01/2024 under the PCR 15 will continue to require publication of the relevant notices for that framework under the PCR 15 until the call-off contract is terminated (for whatever reason), even if the framework itself has ended. This Contract Award Notice is being published in accordance with the requirements for sub-central contracting authorities, NHS Trusts and NHS Foundation Trusts where the contract value is at least £30,000 inclusive of VAT in accordance with the PCR 15.

title: Eclipse Live Provision for NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board
description:

The National GP IT Futures Lot 1 Framework Agreement, against which Call Off Agreements have been executed, have expired on 31 March 2023. title: Award of a call off Contract under the Prison Education Dynamic Purchasing System for Equalities training in Prisons Hertfordshire, Essex, Suffolk
description:

Peer mentor training in equalities, diversity and safeguarding. Herefordshire Essex and Suffolk Prisons Group will commission Diversity, Equalities and Inclusion Training and Prisoner Support in each the below 5 prisons:
-	HMP Chelmsford
-	HMP Highpoint
-	HMP Hollesley Bay
-	HMP Mount
-	HMP Warren Hill

title: Prime Service to General Practice across Suffolk and North East Essex
description:
NHS Suffolk and North East Essex (SNEE) Integrated Care Board (ICB) has awarded a contract to contract to GP Primary Choice Ltd , for the provision of a PRIME Service to General Practice across Suffolk and North East Essex.

The contract commences on 1st April 2024, expiring on 31st March 2025.

A voluntary ex ante transparency notice relating to this matter was published on 28th December 2023 (Notice reference: 2023/S 000-037971), the standstill for which expired midnight on 8th January 2023.

The incumbent provider (GP Primary Choice Ltd) has successfully delivered this service for the past 12 months and has the knowledge, expertise and experience from close working partnerships with General Practice partners that is difficult to develop in a short space of time from any other provider.

This service retains in depth knowledge of the Practices it serves and embedded and trusted relationships with multiple partners, particularly in General Practice teams such as Practice Managers and Practice partners.. The current service provider has become known with local providers and has extremely positive feedback from all partners, which has taken considerable time and effort to obtain. Introducing a new provider risks disrupting these vital links, which would set back the service offer and increase the risks faced by General Practice.

It is well known that mistrust of services within this sector is apparent, hence relationship building has been a key requirement of this service throughout the course of the original pilot. GPPC has worked to develop relationships which support and enable access to key Practice data that assists in the identification and delivery of key quality improvement opportunities within Practices for the benefit of both the Practice and the population. It is believed that introducing a different organisation with different branding to deliver this service would significantly impact the ability to effectively engage with General Practice, due to the need to establish trust with individuals.

The service has experienced and trained staff in place that have worked locally within General Practice and developed that trust with General Practice teams which can flex to the needs of the Practices to maintain best practice throughout the length of the contract.

The ICB deem that changing providers at a time where General Practice are under increasing pressure and facing ever increasing challenges, would have an adverse impact on service delivery for the population that it serves. The ICB is therefore seeking to re-commission the current provider to continue its service delivery for the short duration of the 12 month contract to provide stability in a fragile environment.

The ICB will award the contract utilising the NHS terms and conditions of goods and non-clinical services.

title: In Hours Home Visiting Service - North East Essex
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award by NHS Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB).

The contract award is made to Practice Plus Group for the provision of an In hours Home Visiting Service in North East Essex, from 5 December 2023 to 29 February 2024.

The provider will work with practices to support the creation of additional appointments and free up primary care clinical time in practice, by providing an in hours home visiting service across primary care, using the existing infrastructure offer from the local out of hours service provider. 

It will be resourced through a GP/ANP Team, and visits will be made available through a dedicated referral line staffed by a co-ordinator.  

On receiving, and accepting as an appropriate referral, a home visit would be made by the team of Clinician and Driver.  

The contract value pertaining to this period is up to £60,000. 

The ICB is publishing this Contract Award Notice in the Contracts Finder in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended by The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020) for spend above £30,000.

title: Medical Interoperability Gateway (MIG) - Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board
description:
The purpose of this Notice is to inform the market of a contract awarded to Healthcare Gateway to continue to deliver the Medical Interoperability Gateway (MIG) across Hertfordshire and West Essex. This follows the publication of a Voluntary Ex-Ante Transparency (VEAT) Notice published in FTS on 7th November 2023 (reference: 2023/S 000032983) and observing a voluntary 10-day standstill period following publication.

The new contract will start on 1st January 2024 and will end on 31st December 2024. The value of the new contract is £298,331.57 (inclusive of VAT).

Prior to the incorporation of HWE ICB, Herts Valleys CCG and West Essex CCG had used the tool prior to the ShCR to facilitate sharing of GP information with other providers via a web portal version of the software as well as direct integration. The MIG contracts were previously held by the CCGs on account of the Healthcare Gateway MIG being a niche supplier. A contract award notice was published confirming the previous award of services to 31st May 2023 (reference 2023/S 000-022904).

The total cumulative spend since the contract started is £800,339.62 (inclusive of VAT and excluding the value of this new proposed contract).

The Shared Care Record (ShCR) is used across the Integrated Care System (ICS) to facilitate the sharing of clinical information for the purposes of direct care. Primary Care data from our GP Practices was one of the first datasets that the ICB enabled into the ShCR. This is done via the Healthcare Gateway Medical Interoperability Gateway (MIG) which presents the key GP data into the ShCR for others to see. It is a critical data stream which is evidenced by the high usage data across all datasets being provided by the MIG with an average of over 800,000 transactions per month.

We have undertaken some research into other solutions and have concluded that the MIG is the only available tool which facilitates the sharing of GP data in the way in which it is required. There is no other product currently that offers the functionality and service provision of the MIG. Findings have identified that switching to an alternative provision could result in significant degradation of service and less access to data than we currently surface within the ShCR.

On this basis, we consider Healthcare Gateway to be the only technically capable supplier.

As this was not competitive, the closing date identified in this Notice is the date on which the decision to award the contract to Healthcare Gateway was approved through ICB governance.

title: Stroke Support Service (Life after Stroke) for NHS Mid and South Essex ICB
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Authority, NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs). This Contract Award is made by the Authority to the Stroke Association for the provision of stroke support services (Life after Stroke services) within the Mid and South Essex geographical footprint. 

The contract duration is for 18 months from 01st April 2023 until 30th September 2024. The aggregate contract value is £266,632.00.

The aim of the Stroke Association Service is to provide and coordinate the long-term personalised support that people affected by stroke need to rebuild their lives by enhancing quality of life, increasing social and emotional wellbeing and to prevent further strokes. The Life After Stroke service will provide practical and emotional support to all new stroke survivors and their families/carers, usually up to 12 months post stroke. The service will work in an integrated way with health, social and voluntary sector Providers across the system. The Department of Health National Stroke Strategy (2007) emphasises the need for information to be provided to stroke survivors and their carers, along with support and advice to understand their condition. The impact of a stroke can often last a lifetime and it is critical that people affected receive support in the long-term to ensure they can lead the best possible life. The Stroke Association ensures that people receive the vital input and support they need following a stroke. A third of stroke survivors say that they feel abandoned upon leaving hospital and half report not receiving enough support when they need it. This will be a future focus area for the Stewardship Group. Concerning social impacts, a UK survey (McKevitt, 2011) of self-reported outcomes after stroke found that 52% of stroke survivors experienced a negative change in work activity, 67% a change for the worse in relation to leisure activities or interests, 18% a loss of income, 31% an increase in expenses, and 42% a negative impact on the relationship with their partner. Over half of respondents also reported needing more information about stroke, including diet, applying for benefits, aids and adaptations to the home and driving. It is critical that people affected by stroke receive the support they need in the long-term to rebuild their lives and lead the best life possible. The Stroke Recovery Service ensures that people affected by stroke receive the vital input and support they need.


The Authority is publishing this Contract Award Notice in the Contracts Finder in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended by The Public Procurement (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020) for spend above £30,000.

title: Medical Interoperability Gateway (MIG) - Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board
description:
The purpose of this Notice is to confirm the award of a short-term contract to the incumbent provider, Healthcare Gateway, to deliver the Medical Interoperability Gateway (MIG) across the Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board (HWE ICB).

The Shared Care Record within Hertfordshire and West Essex depends on the MIG to surface GP data from all practices into the Shared Care Record. The HWE ICB is currently undertaking a process to source a long-term solution. This short-term contract is required to ensure that there are continuity of services to allow for the data to continue to flow in the interim.

The contracts have been in place within the Clinical Commissioning Groups prior to the incorporation of the ICB on 1st July 2022. The approximate cumulative value of those contracts is £611,156.

A Notice was published on 23rd January 2023 which provided notification of an extension of the contract to January 2023 (reference 2023/S 000-002024). This has been further extended to end of May 2023 and it&apos;s likely that a further extension will be required to allow the Contracting Authority sufficient time to scope and procure their longer-term requirements for this service.

The value of the additional contract to end of May 2023 is £73,398.80 (including VAT). The market will be informed of any further awards once the long-term planning for the services has been approved through ICB governance.

description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Contracting Authority; NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs).

The contract award is made to Chelmer Medical Partnership for provision of a Polyclinic with an integrated multi-disciplinary team (MDT) for Serious Mental Illness (SMI) across Mid and South Essex. The Polyclinic will run weekly on a Saturday from 9am to 1pm from Tennyson House Surgery and seeks to deliver a full holistic offer to patients with SMI who not only fall into a "Plus 5" cohort, but also fall within the Chelmsford West "Core 20" cohort. title: Emergency Intervention Vehicle - Mental Health Joint Response in Suffolk and North East Essex
description:
This is a Contract Award Notice to communicate a contract award made by the Contracting Authority; Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board, (hereinafter referred to as "the Authority") in compliance with their local standing financial instructions (SFIs).

A Voluntary Ex Ante Transparency notice (VEAT) pertaining to this was published on 17th April 2023. 

In line with the Mental Health Investment Standard, Mental Health Implementation Plan and Long Term Plan investment in provision of mental health specific initiatives should be in place during 23/24 enabling such initiatives as a dedicated joint response vehicle with paramedic and mental health practitioners to be in place to support the Mental Health Crisis and Liaison programme and long term plan priority to reduce ambulance conveyance to Urgent and Emergency Care facilities.
The Mental Health Joint Response car will be delivered in partnership between East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust (EEAST) and Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust (EPUT), with a Paramedic being provided by EEAST, and a Mental Health Practitioner being provided by EPUT.
This will require 2 separate contractual agreements with each provider. The EEAST contract will be a new agreement to support the change in service provision, whereas the EPUT contract will be a variation on the current crisis service contract.
The car will respond to mental and physical health crisis needs in the community and as the pilot has already gathered evidence of success, there is now the requirement to put in place a longer-term commissioning arrangement.

The new contract proposed will be for a period of 36 months with the option to extend for a further 24 months. The new contract will start on 1st April 2023 and will end on 31st March 2026 with the option to extend from 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2028.

The value of this contract without extension is £777,798, increasing to £1,296,330 if extended by a further 24 months.

title: Provision of a Semen Analysis Service
description:
The purpose of this notice is to provide confirmation of the award of a contract to provide a Semen Analysis Service within East and North Hertfordshire and West Essex to its incumbent provider, Herts and Essex Fertility Service.

The service has been in place since February 2017 and is due to end on 31st March 2024.  The new contract will start on 1st April 2024 and will end on 31st March 2026 with the option to extend for a further year.  The total cumulative value of the contract since it started is £300k (excl. VAT and excluding the value of this new contract).  The total value of the new contract is £120,000 (excl. VAT), increasing to £180,000 (excl. VAT) if the option to extend is enacted.

The Semen Analysis service provides post vasectomy and male fertility semen analysis for patients who are registered with an GP within East and North Hertfordshire and West Essex.

The total cumulative value of the service falls below the thresholds for advertisement against The Public Contract Regulations, therefore, the Regulations are not applicable.  The Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board will review the service provision whilst the new contract is in place to understand how best to deliver this service for our patients into the future.

title: Mental Health and Learning Disabilities & Autism Support Framework - reopen 2023
description:
The Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board (SNEE ICB) (the "Commissioners") are issuing this invitation to apply to be listed on the Mental Health and Learning Disabilities & Autism Support Framework (the "Support Framework").

The Support Framework has been established to allow Commissioners to work with named providers to transform and develop mental health services within the boundaries of the Ipswich and East Suffolk, West Suffolk Alliances, and North East Essex Alliance.

The Support Framework forms a list of preferred providers who have declared an interest in one or more of the listed service areas of Crisis, Children, Young People and Families (CYP&F), Community and Learning Disabilities & Autism (LD&A).

The preferred providers listed on the support framework will be approached in the first instance, prior to any open market competition, whenever an opportunity to be involved in the transformation, development and or delivery of mental health and learning disability and autism services is available. 

The Support Framework was established in April 2022 and so far, the preferred providers have been approached regarding the following services:
•	Support for Children & Young People (CYP) in crisis within a hospital or community setting that may require Tier 4 
•	CBT based transdiagnostic resources
•	Mental Health Safe Haven & Wellbeing Hub
•	Suffolk Community Connector Service 
•	Therapeutic Family Service North East Essex
•	Serious Mental Illness & Physical Health - Peer-led Outreach
•	Children & Young Persons Admission Avoidance
•	Mental Health High Intensity Users Service
•	Children & Young Persons Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing System Offer

Mental Health and Wellbeing Services within Suffolk and North East Essex are undergoing a period of transformation and the Support Framework is intended to support these developments by allowing rapid access to providers to support specification development and service delivery.

To apply for this framework you will find details on the In-tend portal https://in-tendhost.co.uk/westsuffolkcommissioning/aspx/Home under the project - Mental Health and Learning Disabilities & Autism Support Framework - reopen 2023. You will need to register with the portal for free and then express an interest in the project to access the application to the Support Framework.
